previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, PTSD, bipolar disorder, and recent ventral hernia repair presented with worsening mid-abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting after being kicked in the abdomen. He was found to have three rim-enhancing fluid collections near his surgical mesh on CT, concerning for abscesses. He was managed conservatively with NPO status, NG tube decompression, IV fluids, and antibiotics. His symptoms improved, nausea resolved, and he tolerated diet advancement to regular food. He remained afebrile with stable vitals and good pain control. He was discharged home on oral pain medications, stool softeners, and instructions to follow up with his surgeon, with clear guidance on when to seek medical attention.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ y/o male with a history of chronic 
pancreatitis s/p multiple abdominal surgeries at BI presenting 
with abdominal pain and vomiting.

# Abdominal Pain: Patient presented to OSH for worsenning of 
chronic abdominal pain and vomiting. Patient was transferred for 
the concern for an internal hernia on CT scan. The surgery team 
evaluated the patient and felt that there was no evidence of 
hernia or SBO. Patient described his symptoms as consistent with 
prior episodes of  pancreatitis. Patient was kept NPO for 2days 
and given dilaudid 2mg q2hours and remained complaining of 
severe abdominal pain.  Patient was given zofran for his nausea 
with adequate resolution. Pt was unable to provide a stool 
sample and studies were not sent. Patient eventually was able to 
tolerate a regular diet without vomiting and was changed to PO 
pain control. Patient stated he was still in pain, but 
consistent with his baseline abdominal pain. Discussion with 
primary care providers described persistent difficulty with his 
pain control and pain prescriptions. Two providers stated 
patient would return after 2 weeks when pt had been given a 
month long prescription, or would complain of pruritis and 
inability to complete the medication prescribed. Patient was 
also not able to obtained appointments from Pain Clinic given he 
had assaulted a fellow in ___. An appointment was made for PCP 
___ at ___.
.  
#syncope: Patient stated he had an episode of LOC a few days 
PTA. Pt described having abdominal pain and nausea. He felt 
lightheaded and had LOC. The description seemed consistent with 
a vasovagal episode.  Patient had no episodes of LOC during 
admission.
.  
# Bipolar Disorder: Patient remained stable and was continued on 
his home regimen of duloxetine and amitriptyline.  
.  
# Hypertension: Blood pressures remained within an acceptable 
range during admission and was continued on home dose of 
lisinopril at 10mg.  
.  
# DM2: Patient's metformin and glargine were held. Patient was 
treated with an insulin sliding scale while in house.
.  
# GERD:Patient was continue on omeprazole.
